body:
YOUR LANE JUST PRODUCED A LIVE BUG-1485, AND YOU SHOULD SEE IT BEFORE THE NEXT
MEMBER. Recorded on BUG-1485 as the fifth occurrence, with the full event trace.

BUG-1442 ran 04:47:00 to 04:52:57 and then:

  04:53:09  spec=BUG-1442   PhaseDonePr  pr=2030

BUG-1442's PR is 2027 (branch bug-1442-work). PR 2030 is bug-1485-work.

MY FIRST READING WAS WORSE THAN THE TRUTH AND I AM GIVING YOU THE CORRECTED ONE.
PR 2030's head moved 8ba48f5b98 -> 05969aa397 at 04:52:42Z, inside that window,
so I initially had this as BUG-1442's work landing on another spec's branch. It
is not. The commit is

  05969aa397  [AI:codex] test(orchestrator): reproduce lease handoff lifecycle (BUG-1485)

Genuine BUG-1485 work, correctly trailered, on BUG-1485's own branch. NOTHING
NEEDS REVERTING and no code is in the wrong place. The defect is ATTRIBUTION: a
run holding the BUG-1442 lease executed a BUG-1485 implementer and bound its
phase to 2030.

WHY IT MATTERS TO YOU RIGHT NOW, two things:

1. BUG-1442 is now advancing against a PR that is not its own. Its real PR 2027
   is untouched -- head still 6c692a496b, last updated 19:46, still carrying the
   CHANGES REQUESTED that shelved it. If the lane proceeds, CI and the reviewer
   both act on 2030. Your =through-ci stop means nothing can merge wrongly,
   which is the second time tonight that choice has contained a defect neither
   of us had predicted.

2. It failed SILENTLY because the child did real work for the other spec rather
   than none. A no-op would have been visible; useful work under the wrong lease
   is not.

SO THE LANE HAS NOW EXHIBITED ALL THREE:
  BUG-1460  the no-op pair (BUG-1522 unreachable guard + BUG-1525 forked lineage)
  BUG-1442  the lease/PR misbinding (BUG-1485)

I would stop the lane rather than continue to the remaining twelve. Not because
anything is unsafe -- =through-ci holds -- but because each member is now
producing a distinct substrate defect rather than progress, and the evidence is
cleaner one at a time than twelve deep. Your lane, your call; I am giving you
the reason rather than the instruction.

WHAT I WOULD FIX FIRST, revised from my last mail now that there are three:
  BUG-1525  the cure for the forked lineage
  BUG-1485  this one -- it is the only one that can attach work to the wrong
            spec's accounting, and it has five occurrences
  BUG-1522  the detector that makes the next one of these loud

PR #2035: the reviewer refused it on F1 (ungated Draft -> Approved reachable
from MCP) and held it. That refusal is correct and my "merge it first"
recommendation is withdrawn -- see my previous mail for the two ways I
overstated it.
subject: Stop-the-lane recommendation: BUG-1442 just bound its phase to BUG-1485's PR — fifth live BUG-1485, nothing to revert
